subsections.subsection_title: 1. Measles — Differential Diagnosis, Features and Complications

items.text: Spreads downwards to trunk and limbs
Rash becomes confluent, particularly on the face
Fever often peaks with the rash
Rash fades in the same order, sometimes with brownish discoloration and fine desquamation
Blindness, especially with vitamin A deficiency
Vitamin A supplementation according to age-specific WHO/national protocol
Treat secondary bacterial infections when indicated
MUAC below 115 mm in children aged 6–59 months
Bilateral pitting nutritional oedema in kwashiorkor
Loss of muscle and subcutaneous fat
Hepatomegaly may occur, particularly in kwashiorkor
Poor breastfeeding or inappropriate complementary feeding
Heart failure from inappropriate fluid or sodium loading
Visual impairment from vitamin A deficiency
Correct electrolytes, especially potassium and magnesium
Avoid excessive sodium and fluid administration
Transition to rehabilitation feeding when stable and appetite improves
Monitor weight, oedema, temperature, glucose and fluid balance

items.text: HPV vaccine: routine vaccination for eligible girls, generally in the 9–14-year age group, according to Nigeria’s programme.
Tetanus-containing vaccines: during pregnancy, according to prior vaccination history and national guidance.
Missed doses: provide catch-up vaccination; do not routinely restart a vaccine series.
Vitamin A is a supplement, not a vaccine.
Certain medications: corticosteroids, antipsychotics, some antiepileptics
Endocrine causes are more likely when obesity is accompanied by reduced linear growth
A fontanelle may transiently appear full when an infant is crying, coughing or lying flat.
Persistent bulging when the infant is calm and upright, especially with fever, vomiting, lethargy or seizures, requires urgent assessment.

subsections.subsection_title: 6. Causes of Delayed and Early Fontanelle Closure

items.text: Severe dehydration may make the fontanelle appear sunken, but does not cause true premature suture fusion

blocks.text: Exam pearl: Fontanelle closure timing varies. Assess head circumference, skull shape, growth and development rather than relying on closure alone.

subsections.subsection_title: 8. ReSoMal and ORS: constituents and osmolality

items.text: ReSoMal: Special rehydration solution for selected children with severe acute malnutrition; use under clinical supervision.
WHO low-osmolarity ORS: Standard oral rehydration solution for diarrhoeal dehydration.
Important: Avoid ReSoMal in suspected cholera or profuse watery diarrhoea because its sodium content is low; use appropriate standard ORS and follow the clinical protocol.
Cerebral palsy in its early hypotonic phase
Crossing upward through head circumference centiles
Diplopia or sixth cranial nerve palsy
Genetic: primary hereditary microcephaly, chromosomal abnormalities, Rett syndrome
Congenital infections: CMV, Zika virus, toxoplasmosis, rubella, syphilis
Brain malformations: lissencephaly, neuronal migration disorders
Prenatal insults: alcohol exposure, teratogenic drugs, maternal malnutrition
Perinatal: severe hypoxic-ischaemic brain injury, intracranial haemorrhage
Postnatal: severe malnutrition, CNS infections, traumatic brain injury
Metabolic: selected inborn errors of metabolism
Craniosynostosis: premature fusion of cranial sutures
Benign enlargement of the subarachnoid spaces
Genetic syndromes: Sotos syndrome, Weaver syndrome, PTEN-related disorders
Metabolic/storage disorders: Canavan disease, Alexander disease, glutaric aciduria type 1
Rickets, occasionally associated with enlarged head size
